_comment: THE single hand-edited source for the portal's visual tokens.
Everything else is generated from this file by tools/gen_tokens.py:
frontend/src/styles/tokens.css  — the React path, imported by base.css
backend/tokens.py               — the Python path, injected by shell.BASE_CSS
frontend/src/lib/tokens.ts      — for colours that must reach JS (recharts
props, inline styles, score bands)
Those three are GENERATED. Edit this file and re-run the generator instead;
tests/test_design_tokens.py fails if they drift.
Token NAMES are deliberately the ones already in use (--bg, --acc, --c-pr...),
not the Constructor Fabric --color-* names. Renaming is a separate, visible
step — see docs/design-system.md. This file exists so that step is one edit.
`themes` is a map so a dark theme is additive: add a `dark` key with the same
token names and the generator emits its block too. Absent today.
`text_on` names the surfaces a colour is used as BODY TEXT on. The contrast
test derives its WCAG AA pairs from it. Non-text use (icons, borders, chart
fills) is not asserted yet.
VALUES ARE VERBATIM what shipped before consolidation. Several are near-
duplicates that a design pass should collapse, and they are kept apart here
because collapsing them changes pixels:
#8b5cf6 lives under four names: --app, --violet, --c-loc, --c-epic, --cat-task
--acc-soft #edecfe and --acc-bg #eeeefe are two lavenders one apart
chart/* and category/* overlap on five hues but disagree on epic
See docs/design-system.md for the list and why each is still separate.

panel2.note: inset surface — code, table head, chips

bad-soft.note: the failed-to-load card's fill (set from TS)

acc-bg.note: accent surface, identity page's one-off shade

swatch-empty.note: a work-type with no colour set yet

company-empty.note: a company with no colour pinned or derived

category._note: The taxonomy wizard's work-category swatches — a SEPARATE palette from chart/*, consumed by name from SemanticWizard.tsx. It agrees with chart/* on five hues and disagrees on epic (#5b5bf0 here, #8b5cf6 there); that disagreement predates this file and is preserved rather than silently resolved.

status._note: Badge, pill and row surfaces. These are the pre-redesign GitHub-ish semantic pairs, and they are NOT the same values as --good/--good-bg etc — a pill's green surface (#dafbe1) and the card's (#e7f6ee) have always differed. Kept apart because unifying them changes pixels; unifying is a step-5 design call.

tooltip-bg.note: tooltip and log surfaces — dark, so text on it is --on-solid

chat-tool-bg.note: tool-call block in the chat log

option-fg.note: native <option> text, which ignores most inherited colour

score._note: Developer-score bands (widgets/score/PersonScore). Read from TS, never from CSS.

palettes._note: Colours handed out in code rather than referenced from CSS — a chart series' `color` in an API payload, a score band, an index-assigned swatch. Both the frontend (lib/tokens.ts) and the backend (backend/tokens.py VALUES/palettes) read these from here. A list's ORDER is load-bearing: it decides which colour something gets by index, so appending is safe and reordering repaints existing items.

company_palette._note: Company series colours, assigned by a name-derived hash (store.company_color_map) so a company keeps its colour as ranks change. The teal was #0a7ea4, which sat 58 units from the blue in RGB — close enough that two adjacent series read as one colour; #14b8a6 is 95 from its nearest neighbour.

series_colors._note: One-off named series in specific charts. The frontend legend swatches in Trend.tsx mirror `opened`/`merged`, so both sides now read the same entry instead of two hand-matched literals.

on_primary._comment: Foreground used on a filled --acc surface. Checked by the contrast test.
